passages: Ultrasound features suspicious for malignancy include irregular shape, non-parallel (taller-than-wide) orientation, angular or spiculated margins, posterior acoustic shadowing, and associated architectural distortion or calcifications. These findings correspond to BI-RADS 4C or 5 assessment and require tissue sampling via core needle biopsy.

BI-RADS 5 (highly suggestive of malignancy) is assigned when the lesion displays a combination of classic malignant features with a positive predictive value ≥95%. Appropriate management includes tissue diagnosis prior to definitive surgical planning.

guidelines.source: ACR BI-RADS 5th Edition — Benign Ultrasound Assessment
passages: Features of a classic benign lesion (BI-RADS 2) on ultrasound include oval shape, parallel orientation, circumscribed margins, and absent or mild posterior acoustic enhancement. Simple cysts must meet all criteria: anechoic, round or oval, circumscribed, thin imperceptible wall, and posterior acoustic enhancement.

BI-RADS 3 (probably benign) is assigned to solid lesions with a circumscribed oval shape and parallel orientation without suspicious features, carrying a malignancy risk <2%. Short-interval follow-up at 6 months is recommended, with subsequent follow-up at 6-month intervals for 2 years to establish stability.

guidelines.source: ACR Practice Parameter 2020 — Breast Ultrasound Examination
passages: A normal breast ultrasound demonstrates homogeneous echotexture of the breast parenchyma with well-defined layers: skin, subcutaneous fat, mammary zone (fibroglandular tissue), retromammary fat, and pectoral muscle. No focal solid or cystic masses, architectural distortion, or suspicious calcifications are identified.

Supplemental breast ultrasound screening is recommended for women with dense breast tissue (ACR density categories C or D) who are at average or intermediate risk, as mammographic sensitivity is reduced in dense breasts. Automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) systems are FDA-approved for this purpose.
